messages.subject: hcfa() problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I have been trying to do an hcfa() with the following data (.csv, raw
data, 624 observations of 9 variables):

MEMBER	SIDE	OBLIGEE	RHETOBL	CONTRAST	VALUES	WESTRAT	IMPLIC	MODAL
Abbott	o	x	n	y	n	n	x	s
Abbott	o	d	y	n	n	n	x	s
Abbott	o	d	y	n	n	n	x	s
Adams	g	x	n	n	n	n	x	s
Albanese	g	x	n	n	n	n	x	s
Albanese	g	d	n	y	n	n	x	s
Andrews	o	d	n	y	n	n	y	s
Andrews	o	x	n	n	n	n	x	s
AnnetteEllis	g	x	n	n	y	y	x	s
AnthonySmith	o	x	n	y	n	n	n	s
...

hcfa() creates the subtables but I get the following error message
when I choose files for the analysis:

Enter one or more numbers separated by spaces, or an empty line to
cancel
1: 1 2 3 4 5 1022
1done, 5to go ...
Error in Summary.factor(c(4L, 2L, 3L, 3L, 2L, 2L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 5L,
5L,  :
  sum not meaningful for factors
In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the
first 50)
warnings()
1: In scan(file, what, nmax, sep, dec, quote, skip, nlines,  ... :
  number of items read is not a multiple of the number of columns
2: In names(sub.table)[-length(names(sub.table))] <-
colnames(data.all[which(table.chooser[i,  ... :
  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length
...

The first column contains 120 different names and I thought this could
cause the problem. Leaving it out does not help.

Thank you for your help!!

Theresa

messages.subject: hcfa(): Q value
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,
I keep getting very high Q values in hcfa() results – they are way
beyond 1, sometimes up to 46 or 48. I am a bit puzzled since according
to Krauth/Lienert (1973/1995: 34), Q should always be between 0 and 1,
and I therefore hesitate to take it as evidence of a particularly
strong configuration in my data... Is the Q in hcfa() not the same Q
as in Krauth/Lienert? Or is there anything wrong with my data?

Best
Thomas
